newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end lower ahead of options expiry.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end lower ahead of options expiry.

text.p: FCOJ futures plunged sharply lower near the close as speculators liquidated long positions accumulated since the Jan 19 freeze in Florida, traders said.
Locals with offset options positions are also believed to be holding long positions, and March options expire today, Merrill Lynch noted in its weekly citrus comment.
March settled down 1.75 at 83.30 cents, having ranged from 85.65 to 82.75 cents. The back months settled 2.10 lower to 1.30 higher. Volume was estimated at 5,000 lots.

An Arctic airmass that could hit Florida by the end of next week is not expected to cause a freeze, meteorologists said. Previously, they said the weather could threaten the crop with freezing temperatures.
Trade had remained cautious for most of the session as players squared positions ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's crop production estimate Wednesday.

Merrill Lynch said the USDA is not likely to reduce the crop by more than 15 million boxes from its previous estimate of 220 million 90-lb boxes. Yields could fall to 1.50 gallons per box from 1.60 gallons prior to the freeze, it said.
